- Scaly rash present on scalp and forehead — matches typical distribution of seborrheic dermatitis  
- No “black dots” observed or reported — highly specific finding against tinea capitis  
- Skin scraping microscopy shows no fungal elements — rules out dermatophyte infection  
- Skin scraping culture shows no bacterial growth — rules out primary bacterial infection  
- Diagnosis is explicitly stated as “Seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap)” in the Final Clinical Assessment  

[GAPS]  
- Morphology details (e.g., greasy, yellow, thick, adherent, erythematous) are not specified — limits confidence in distinguishing from other scaly conditions like mild psoriasis or early atopic dermatitis  
- Presence or absence of erythema, induration, or oozing is not described — key for assessing inflammation or secondary infection  
- Pruritus is “uncertain” — limits assessment for atopic or contact etiologies  
- Alopecia is “not reported” — not confirmed absent; therefore cannot rule out early tinea capitis with minimal hair loss  
- Extra-scalp involvement is “not recalled” — insufficient to confirm confinement to scalp/forehead  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Seborrheic dermatitis
